title: Organization & Leveling Framework
subtitle: M&S Mechanical / Soluciones BIM · 2027 target operating model
footer: MS Systems · Organization & Leveling Framework 2027 (DRAFT v1) — prepared by HR for leadership approval. Line accent colours for VDC Lab and Permit My House are placeholders pending each line's brand kit. Not legal or tax advice; jurisdiction-specific items flagged for local counsel.

seniority.heading: Seniority & leveling model
seniority.intro: One ladder across every discipline and line, so a "Senior" in VDC Lab, MEPHub or Permit My House means the same thing. Level = how much experience/autonomy a person has. Role = what they are accountable for. The two are separate on purpose — that is what fixes the old "PM means both a rank and a job" confusion.

levels.name: Executive
fields: Sets direction for the whole company.
Leads directors and the leadership team.

levels.name: Director
fields: Owns a whole service line or major shared function.
Accountable for outcomes, growth & P&L-style performance of their domain.
Full professional fluency; client & partner facing.
VDC Lab Director, MEPHub Director, People & Culture Director, PMO Director.

levels.name: Manager
fields: Owns a discipline (Discipline Manager) OR projects (PM) OR a shared function.
Full accountability for a team or a portfolio of work.
Manages Leads and producers / drives project teams.
Advanced — leads calls, meetings, client comms.
Mechanical Discipline Manager, Project Manager, Estimating Manager.

levels.name: Lead
levels.kind: TOP INDIVIDUAL CONTRIBUTOR · ENTRY TO MANAGEMENT FORK

Mechanical Drafting Lead, Lead Electrical Engineer, Training Lead.

fields: Owns own deliverables end to end; 3 systems, deep in ≥1.

tracks.title: Dual track from L4 up
tracks.kind: GROW WITHOUT FORCING EVERYONE INTO MANAGEMENT
bullets: Technical track: Lead → Principal / Specialist. Deep expert who sets standards and solves the hardest technical problems — no direct reports required.
Management track: Discipline Manager → Director. Accountable for people, capacity and outcomes of a discipline or line.
Both tracks are paid and valued equivalently at the same level. People can move between them.

tracks.title: PE track (MEPHub)
bullets: Junior Engineer collects qualifying experience → Mid → Senior (PE in progress) → Lead PE → Discipline Manager (PE).
Roles that require or track a US Professional Engineer licence are flagged PE on the chart.
Licensure timelines and reciprocity vary by US state — confirm with local counsel; HR tracks progress, not legal status.

workModel: Work model, pulled out of job descriptions into policy. In the legacy docs, work-from-home was written into each role ("no trabajo en casa", "1 día"). That is a policy, not a competency, so it now lives here: L1–L2 primarily on-site, L3 up to 1 fixed remote day, L4+ hybrid/flexible — all subject to US vs. Colombia location rules per role, which we set case by case. Jurisdiction-specific labour/tax items are flagged for local counsel.

leveling.name: Lead

Sets standards, reviews and approves work for release. This is the fork: technical track (Principal / Specialist) or management (Discipline Manager). Goal: own the craft, quality and delivery of your pod.

rows.label: Technical mastery
values: The technical authority for your pod; deep, broad proficiency — the person others come to

rows.label: Software & tools

rows.label: Autonomy
values: Owns release for the pod — the final approval to issue any deliverable (drawings, models, calcs or coordination) and accountable for what ships. Makes the technical calls; escalates only cross-discipline / business issues

(From Mid, people “ghost” English meetings to build spoken confidence early.) Goal: the department's technical reference — ready for Lead or the Principal track.

Recognized expert in your department; solves the hardest technical problems

roles.title: Mechanical MEP Designer
roles.meta: Department: Mechanical Discipline · Reports to: Mechanical MEP Design Lead → Mechanical Discipline Manager (VDC Lab) · Levels: Junior (L1) · Mid (L2) · Senior (L3) — per the company Leveling Model.

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: Produces fabrication-level mechanical shop drawings and BIM models for the U.S. construction market — turning engineering intent into precise, coordinated, buildable deliverables, within VDC Lab standards and the estimated hours.

sections.title: Key responsibilities
bullets: Model and draft mechanical systems (HVAC ductwork, piping, equipment) in Revit and AutoCAD to fabrication level of detail.
Produce coordinated, standards-compliant shop drawings and sheets from engineering documents and markups.
Incorporate redlines/markups accurately; keep models and drawings clean and to company standards.
Participate in multi-trade BIM coordination and clash resolution; use 3D point-cloud / scan data where provided.
Self-check against checklists before review; correct QA/QC feedback.
Log time accurately, deliver within estimated hours, and raise overrun risk early.

sections.title: Level expectations
pairs: Assists on routine tasks; supervised; learning standards, systems and the software stack.
Owns standard deliverables end-to-end with light oversight; proficient across the tools.
Owns complex, non-standard packages; a technical go-to and mentor; first client contact.

sections.title: Required competencies
pairs: Proficiency in the mechanical discipline (HVAC ductwork, piping, equipment, fabrication practices), appropriate to level.
Revit, AutoCAD, Navisworks, Autodesk Forma, 3D point clouds — learning the stack at Junior, mastery growing through Senior.

All work is in English; reading comprehension is a hiring gate. Junior writes notes/keynotes with AI help; Mid writes clear notes independently; Senior is comfortable on calls/meetings and first client contact.
Junior: supervised, work reviewed → Mid: independent on standard scope → Senior: owns complex work end-to-end and collaborates with peers on the hardest problems.
Works to the estimated hours and logs time cleanly; grows from working within the estimate to planning own work to the fee. Protecting project profitability is part of the role at every level.

sections.title: Nice to have
bullets: Fabrication or field experience in mechanical systems.
Custom Revit families / LOD 350–400 modeling.
Familiarity with U.S. codes and coordination workflows.
Conversational spoken English.

sections.title: Location & work model
paragraphs: Colombia or U.S. per position. Work model per policy: L1–L2 primarily on-site, L3 up to one fixed remote day. Employment terms confirmed with local counsel.

ladder.title: MS Systems — Career Growth Ladder
ladder.intro: How people grow here. Each band has internal steps so progress is recognized often — a small, earned promotion, not automatic tenure. At Senior the path forks: keep growing technically toward Lead, or move into delivery as a Project Manager. It's the path you choose — both are valued and paid the same at each level.

steps.name: GM / COO
steps.text: Runs the company day to day; aligns the lines & shared functions.

steps.name: CEO
steps.text: Owns strategy, capital, growth & the top relationships.

steps.name: Director I
steps.text: Owns a whole line or major function — its people, quality, growth & P&L.

steps.name: Director II
steps.text: Owns a larger multi-line domain or the most strategic function.

items.text: ▲ both tracks lead up to Director ▲

items.name: Discipline Manager

steps.name: Manager I
steps.text: Owns one discipline — its people, capacity, standards & margin.

steps.name: Manager II
steps.text: Runs a larger / multi-pod discipline at scale; develops Leads.

notes: Deep-technical alternative: Principal / Specialist — same level, no people-management.

steps.name: Lead I
steps.text: Technical authority for a pod; reviews & signs off, sets standards, mentors.

steps.name: Lead II
steps.text: Owns the craft & standards across pods / a discipline; grooms future leads.

steps.name: Senior PM
steps.text: Owns the largest / most complex or multi-line projects & key accounts.

steps.name: Project Manager
steps.text: Owns projects end-to-end — scope, schedule, budget, client, coordination, invoicing & change orders.

items.text: Fork at Senior (L3). From Senior you pick your track — Lead (own the craft, quality & delivery of a pod → Discipline Manager or Principal) or Project Manager (own projects end-to-end → Senior PM). Same level, same pay band; switch tracks later by agreement.

steps.name: Senior I
steps.text: Owns complex deliverables end-to-end, unsupervised; mentors juniors.

steps.name: Senior II
steps.text: A recognized expert; trusted on the hardest work; sets local best practice.

steps.name: Senior III
steps.text: The department's technical go-to; drives quality & standards; understands the project budget.
steps.next: Choose a path — Lead or PM

steps.name: Mid I
steps.text: Handles standard deliverables end-to-end with light oversight.

steps.name: Mid II
steps.text: Well-rounded; anticipates coordination; minimal review on standard work.

steps.name: Mid III
steps.text: Takes on complex / non-standard tasks; a quality reference for juniors.

steps.name: Junior I
steps.text: Onboarding: learns standards & core software; fully supervised.

steps.name: Junior II
steps.text: Completes routine, well-defined tasks with light review.

steps.name: Junior III
steps.text: Delivers routine packages independently; consistent quality on standard scope.

ladder.footnote: Steps are a leveling & compensation layer — they live in HR records and reviews, not on the org chart or client deliverables. Lead (L4) and Project Manager / Discipline Manager (L5) are paid on the same bands per the compensation structure. Pay figures are set per the company pay bands and confirmed with local counsel.

sizing.intro: Set the span-of-control ratios and the producer demand per discipline. The management layers — Leads, Discipline Managers, Directors, QA/QC and PMs — size themselves. Watch the direct-to-overhead ratio to keep it lean.

scorecard.intro: Built on the Leveling Model. Promotion mode rates against a chosen step; hiring mode reads the level from the ratings.

Minimal supervision on standard deliverables; makes routine decisions — work is still checked before release

Rework is rare; catches own errors before review; applies standards unprompted

A go-to peer; mentors juniors, helps onboard; may lead a small task
Holds the budget on harder work; works to the hours set by Estimating and flags early when a task runs long; starts to see how their piece fits the overall project budget, not just their own hours

steps.label: Senior I
exp: Deep, dependable proficiency in your department; owns complex work confidently
Expert user — deep command of the tools and highly efficient; improves their own workflow and helps teammates when they get stuck
Produces complex work with little supervision; still routed through the Lead for release
Owns complex, non-standard deliverables end-to-end
Sets the quality bar by example; catches issues others miss

Deep comprehension; writes clean, professional English on deliverables and in written client correspondence (emails, RFIs) when needed. An active listener on client / technical calls who speaks up on familiar points.
Actively mentors juniors & mids; a trusted informal leader

steps.label: Senior II
exp: Recognized expert in your department; solves the hardest technical problems
Solves the hard, non-standard software problems for the team; sets up and improves the shared ways of working in the tools and shows others how
The Lead may trust them to deliver — including to clients — as a judgement call; the Lead remains accountable

Reviews others' work; defines local best practice & checklists

Coaches the pod; may lead a small team or workstream

Reliably protects the budget on complex work; when asked, gives the Estimating team technical input on complex or non-standard scope, and flags out-of-scope / extra work early to the PM as a potential change order

steps.label: Senior III
exp: The technical reference for your department; shapes how the work is done

The person the team turns to when they're stuck in the software — the recognized software reference for the discipline. You get here by consistently solving problems others can't, sharing what you learn, and picking up new or adjacent tools as projects require

Consistently produces work at the quality needed to go out the door; the natural bridge to Lead, who gives the final approval to issue any deliverable — drawings, models, calculations or coordination, across VDC Lab and MEPHub

Owns the department's quality standards in practice; drives continuous improvement
